question: Is the q4 attention kernel at 250K instruction-bound (the dequant) or bandwidth-bound, before any tensor-core work? (PLAN 14.10's tensor-core item, its first step: 'measure the dequant limiter with cuda_inkc_bench')
box: RTX 5070 12 GB sm_120, CUDA 13.4; one GPU process at a time
chunk_is: one layer's global attention on a 1,024-row prompt chunk at its end (the widest chunk; the average over a 250K prefill's 244 chunks is about half this)

decode_cells.note: one decode step over a 250K prefix

reading: q4 reads 6.4x fewer bytes than f32 and takes 34% less time, so the mirror's bytes are not what limits it: at f32 the kernel reaches 246 GB/s (the card's own read rate) while at q4 it reaches 58.6 GB/s, i.e. it spends about four fifths of its time unpacking, not reading. The bandwidth ceiling for q4's 39.8 GiB is ~0.17 s against the measured 0.73 s, so the dequant is the limiter with a 4.3x headroom.
consequence: the tensor-core item's premise holds and its gate is now measured: an mma port must ship with a vectorized unpack (as PLAN 14 says), because the unpack, not the loads or the FLOPs, is what the 4.5 TFLOP/s q4 number is made of. At the engine's 250K cell the kernel is ~673 s of the 836 s device side (PLAN 14.9); a 4x kernel would leave ~168 s, and the expert path at the microbench's 99 s would then be the next floor. This is a measurement of the limiter only: no kernel was written.
next: the vectorized q4/q8 unpack (P5's arithmetic, an explicit 4-bit LUT-free dequant into 16-bit lanes) and then the mma over the same blocks, gated by the CPU reference (tests/test_cuda_inkc.cu) and the needle
